bullets: description: Presents an actual patient case with a specific disease or condition with an accompanying clinical image, followed by a multiple-choice question ('What Would You Do Next?' with 4 single-phrase plausible treatment options describing possible courses of action) and a brief discussion.

limits: body up to 850 words (Total: no more than 250 words for the case presentation, question, and 4 one-sentence answers, followed by no more than 600 words for the diagnosis and discussion (no more than 500 words if the discussion includes a Figure))
limits: no abstract and no Key Points
limits: up to 10 references
limits: up to 2 figures
limits: up to 3 authors
limits: title up to 60 characters including spaces
components: required sections: Case Presentation, Diagnosis and Discussion
components: signed JAMA Network Patient Permission form for any identifiable patient
components: cover letter — complete contact information for the corresponding author and whether the authors have published, posted, or submitted any related papers from the same study
format: submit a Word document (not PDF); 10-, 11-, or 12-point font, double-spaced, right margins unjustified (ragged).
format: title page, abstract, text, references, figure legends and tables each start on a new page, numbered consecutively from the title page.

format: title page carries the title, every author's full name, highest academic degrees and affiliations, the corresponding author's complete contact information, and the manuscript word count (not including title, abstract, acknowledgment, references, tables, and figure legends).

format: AMA Manual of Style, 11th edition — references numbered in order of first citation, cited with superscript Arabic numerals; up to 6 authors listed, otherwise the first 3 and et al.; journal names abbreviated per PubMed.
format: tables at the end of the manuscript file, numbered in citation order, titles of 10–15 words, 10- or 12-point single-spaced, never as images.

format: each figure a separate file of at most 1 MB; photographs and illustrations at least 350 ppi, line drawings at least 600 ppi; no pie charts, 3-D graphs or stacked bar charts; avoid more than 4 panels.
format: individual files should stay under 500 kB and must not exceed 1 MB; the whole submission under 5 MB (video excluded).
extra: Do not include the patient's race, ethnicity, or country of origin in the title or the first line of the article.
extra: The journal wants 'common problems presenting uncommonly, rather than unusual or rare conditions (ie, "zebras")'.
extra: Manuscripts not meeting these guidelines will not be considered.
extra: Table row gives 'Discussion: 500-600 words' and '1-2 small figures'.
extra: If the Figure includes a Video, see the Multimedia guidance.
extra: 4 single-phrase plausible options with 1 being preferred.
extra: No more than 2 small figures totaling 3 image components (Figure 1 ≤2 components for the case presentation; Figure 2 ≤1 component for the diagnosis and discussion).
extra: Short title that describes the disease entity or case presentation and does not include the diagnosis.
extra: Image and case presentation from the same patient and not previously published.
extra: Original image file minimum resolution 350 dpi at a width of about 5 inches.
extra: At least 1 author, ideally the corresponding author, with sufficient expertise and experience with the topic.
extra: this summary is the app's distillation — open the author instructions above to confirm against the journal's current text.
